The interlinear replacement is provisionally read récipro and is attached to the surviving right-hand que. Its compressed letters and overlap with the old line remain uncertain. The small low mark before q may be the o of the replacement rather than punctuation; no extra period is asserted.

Two separate horizontal strokes occur between les and hypothèses; they are preserved as an equals-like sign, not expanded to a word. Read loc. and i.e. literally. At the right end the old i.e. is visibly crossed.

The live difference is overline(X_J-star) setminus X_J-star. The inserted equality reads X_(bar J setminus J)-star; the bar belongs only to its first subscript J. Its curved leader attaches the equality to the preceding difference before soit. The larger apparent radical-like stroke above the small insertion is part of the preceding word que, not a mathematical radical or overbar.

The short form f et s appears twice, with a stop after s in the upper occurrence only. The line is transcribed literally despite its repeated phrasing. The upper i.e has no securely separate terminal stop, while the lower i.e. does. loc has a raised t, not a written expansion.

The canceled short phrase reads donc les. The following slanted sentence crosses the lower box boundary: Soit maintenant is retained only tentatively because lower portions are cut. pour, the quantifier/index clause and le remain identifiable. The low terminal noun after pro- favors pro-voisinage, with a late descender and low final return, but the compressed word remains uncertain.

The marginal arrow has a hooked left tail and a small pointed right endpoint. Its separate parenthesized label is a tilde with h above it. The upper decoration on X_i is a dark slanted solid mark; star is favored, but a prime-like reading cannot be fully excluded. Both prose lines and the parenthetical X métrisable are retained.
